column8: Low-risk at 11 weeks, weighing home, midwife-led or OB-led birth after reading frightening accounts.
column9: I have read many informative but frightening experiences of women having traumatizing birth experiences in hospitals, even with midwives. Even with homebirths with a midwife.

column8: What she wants from interviewing midwives and birth centres.
column9: I want to ask all the right questions and be super thorough while interviewing midwives/centers to make sure I increase my chances as much as possible for a non traumatic birth. I am very big on respect for autonomy and informed consent.

column8: Replying to a commenter about trusting her care team.
column9: I wish I knew exactly what questions I need to ask so that I can feel assured I am trusting the right people.

column8: What she wants instead of social media.
column9: I want off of social media, and to have a provider I can trust for information and guidance! Social media is exhausting. So much contrasting info and emotional jolts

column8: Steps she is taking now to prepare for after the birth.
column9: I am very concerned about the postpartum and have been taking steps to try to prepare for an easier post partum. Trying to find remote work, more friends and social support, hopefully a therapist who is really compatible with me (it's been so hard to find one).

column8: Her question back to a commenter who had given birth.
column9: What are some things that you found most helpful during post partum? If you did it again what type of preparations or resources would be most important to you?

column8: Three weeks after her second baby, wanting to stop pumping around the clock.
column9: I exclusively pumped my first born and it’s so hard to get away from counting and monitoring every ounce.😩😵‍💫

column8: At 21 weeks on very early shifts and long runs of workdays.
column9: I am 21 weeks, and have never been this exhausted in my life. And morning sickness is making a return? I work 4am-12am. I live a half hour away from my job so I usually wake up around 2:30 am.
I just worked 7 days in a row had two days off, now I have another 7 in a row to work.

column8: A week after a positive test in a planned pregnancy, she feels numb rather than happy.
column9: I can only think about all the changes ahead, the challenges, and how much everything will change between my partner and me.

column8: Living abroad; her mother demanded to know on a video call whether she was pregnant before she was ready.
column9: My mum asked me to “swear” I wasn’t lying, and I felt cornered and interrogated. I wasn’t far enough along to announce anything, so I ended up lying because I felt like I had no other option.

column8: How she wanted to share the news.
column9: I’ve always said that when I have news, I want to share it in my own time, and ideally tell both my family and in-laws at the same time so no one feels excluded.

column8: Dreading a planned long trip home.
column9: I’m now dreading an upcoming long visit back to the UK because I don’t even feel like I want to spend time with my family or in-laws right now.

column8: Called a preschool with a long waitlist as soon as she was pregnant, before telling family.
column9: It also has an insane waitlist and I was always told to call as soon as I was pregnant so I did and I spoke to the director. I told her it was early and we weren’t telling people yet.

column8: The director told an ex-friend; she fears raising it.
column9: I’m afraid if I tell her I didn’t want the friend to know and call her out about it, I won’t end up with a spot.

column8: Aside about using a chatbot in an old friendship dispute.
column9: I put all our texts into ChatGPT (before I knew it was bad)
